mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 4.5% signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in demand, triggering a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 100.0 indicates manufacturing supply chain disruption that squeezes corporate profits through higher input costs and reduced output, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level above 1.1 million units indicates strong consumer confidence and economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1.1 million.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly nonfarm payrolls increase exceeding 200,000 jobs signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicate a monetary policy tightening causing economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During a Federal Reserve hiking cycle (consecutive monthly FEDFUNDS increases), higher borrowing costs dampen corporate investment and consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances during consecutive monthly FEDFUNDS increases.
